controls.summary: Created a worldwide license requirement for 3A090.a/4A090.a/.z items and a model-weights control, with a compliance date of 2025-05-15. On 2025-05-13 BIS announced rescission and non-enforcement. As of the 2026-07-14 UAE rule, the §742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) text remains in the EAR but BIS enforces it only for D:1/D:4/D:5 (excluding A:5/A:6) destinations and D:5/Macau-headquartered entities. A Federal Register rule formally rescinding the framework was not found (see gaps). Status 'rescinded' reflects the agency's announced rescission/non-enforcement.

evidence.quote: With this IFR, BIS establishes a worldwide license requirement for ECCNs 3A090.a, 4A090.a, and corresponding .z items in new § 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A).

controls.instrument: License requirement communicated to exporters by U.S. Government notification ('is informed'), not published in the Federal Register
items: NVIDIA H20 and ICs achieving H20 memory/interconnect bandwidth
applies_to: *entities headquartered in / parented in those destinations
controls.summary: USG informed NVIDIA on 2025-04-09 (and 2025-04-14, 'indefinite future') and AMD that exports of H20/MI308-class products to China and D:5 require a license. NVIDIA reports USG granted some H20 licenses in August 2025 and that USG officials expected 15% of licensed H20 revenue, with no regulation codifying it. Superseded in practice by the January 2026 case-by-case policy for chips below TPP 21,000 / 6,500 GB/s.

evidence.quote: the USG requires a license for export to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, or to companies headquartered or with an ultimate parent therein, of the Company’s H20 integrated circuits and any other circuits achieving the H20’s memory bandwidth, interconnect bandwidth, or combination thereof
The Export Control applies to the Company’s MI308 products.
In August 2025, the USG granted licenses that would allow us to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers

USG officials have expressed an expectation that the USG will receive 15% of the revenue generated from licensed H20 sales, but to date, the USG has not published a regulation codifying such requirement.

controls.instrument: Final rule: Revision to License Review Policy for Advanced Computing Commodities
items: advanced computing commodities with TPP < 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth < 6,500 GB/s (e.g., NVIDIA H200, AMD MI325X)
controls.summary: Moves license review for exports from the U.S. of chips below TPP 21,000 / 6,500 GB/s to end users in China or Macau from presumption of denial to case-by-case, conditioned on supply certifications, a 50% cap relative to U.S. shipments, KYC, and U.S. third-party testing. Reexports and D:5-headquartered entities elsewhere remain presumption of denial. NVIDIA reports licenses granted from Feb 2026 and a 25% tariff on inspected H200s under Proclamation 11002.

evidence.quote: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising its license review policy for exports of certain semiconductors to China and Macau—changing it from a presumption of denial to a case-by-case review.
the aggregate shipments of the product to China and Macau will be no more than 50% of the total product shipped to customers for end use in the United States of that product
The effective date of this rule is January 15, 2026.
Beginning in February 2026, the USG granted licenses that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers, but such sales were restricted by the PRC government

gaps.topic: Formal Federal Register rescission of the AI Diffusion rule (90 FR 4544)
gaps.why: A search of Federal Register BIS rules through 2026-09-24 found no rule formally rescinding the framework; BIS's 2025-05-13 release says a formalizing regulation is planned, and the 2026-07-14 UAE rule describes non-enforcement under guidance.
gaps.would_need: A published BIS rule removing §742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) worldwide requirement / tiering, or an eCFR history showing its removal.

gaps.why: Only NVIDIA's 10-Q statement that USG officials 'expressed an expectation' of 15%; no regulation, license condition text or agreement was found.
gaps.would_need: Published BIS license conditions or an agreement between USG and NVIDIA/AMD.
